intent.note: R44 ('drop tk2s; when os.symlink is refused call _harness.skip(check, tk2l, <mechanism with the reason>, True) as tests/test__config.py does'): tests/test__evidence_io.py removes tk2s and adds `if link_skip is not None: _harness.skip(check, "tk2l", "os.symlink is refused here (%s), so the tree stayed plain and no symlink-reached tree was recorded" % (link_skip,), True)`. The label starts SKIPPED HERE with the id at the front, the OSError/NotImplementedError/AttributeError text is in the mechanism, and the skip is emitted only on the refusal branch, where linked is None and the tk2l RED-FIRST check is not emitted. This is the same shape as tests/test__config.py:3033. A refused symlink is therefore a named skip and no longer a green check that could not fail. grep of the task tree finds no remaining tk2s outside the journal and returns records. R42 ('reword the _BUILD_DELAY judged-literal row to claim only what holds'): I read the row against _build_counted (test_stamp_verification.py:1990-2004). The bound is built + deadline - delay/2. A correct helper is killed at its own start plus the deadline, so its last sign of life is under the bound and no interpreter start or CPU starvation moves it later. A mutant granting a fresh timeout at the spawn is cut at no earlier than built + deadline with its last beat within one beat of the cut, so it ends delay/2 - beat over the bound. The new row says exactly that, limits the margin to an unloaded runner, concedes that a starved child can miss its last beats and let the mutant through, and ends 'a slow runner can hide the mutant but never fail a correct helper'. The old over-claim (stays that far over the bound 'however slow the runner') is gone. The reference to the _BEAT row is fair: that row says a slower beat can let a mutated helper pass, never fail a correct one. R35 ('pw5 windows disjunct asserts the spelling it exercised or records a named skip, never passes silently'): tools/prove-gates.py:4111-4118 replaces `respelled is None and os.name == "nt"` with the same test plus len(still)==1, killed not None, and _canonical_path(still[0]) == _canonical_path(killed["trees"][0]). So on Windows with the link refused, pw5 passes only when the one registration git lists resolves to the pool's own worker tree. The label already prints 'NOT exercised' for that branch. Where respelled is None and os is not nt the case is still red, as before. This takes the 'assert' option, not the 'skip' option, which the clause allows. The disjunct is not vacuous, because still is a list and can never equal [None]. Claim vs diff: the outcome describes the three hunks accurately and the descriptive line is true. The executor's 'tk2s no longer exists' and the dependants answer hold: no defined name used elsewhere (_cases, _selftest, _fs_row, _crlf_cases, _scan, ...) changed, and the ids tk2o/tk2t/tk3/sk1/pw5 are kept. Edits are confined to the three declared files; no F/P/BUG ids were added to code. Not verified by me: the claim that the scratch drivers went red/green. I did not run the suite (the gate ran and is my input).
intent.redFirstBasis: The executor filed not-attempted: a regression task (expectRedFirst false). It offers scratch drivers instead of a shared-tree red run: pw5's None-spelling branch with the link refused, os.name patched to nt and _canonical_path made to disagree went False while the old disjunct stayed True; tk2l printed 'SKIPPED HERE - os.symlink is refused here (OSError: no privilege)' with os.symlink raising and 'RED-FIRST' with symlinks working. No command or exit code is recorded for those drivers and they are not in the tree, so I read them as an unreproducible claim, not as a proved red. By reading, the pw5 mutation is plausible (the old disjunct had no content check) and the tk2l skip branch follows from the code. The sk1 row is prose, and no case can fail on its wording.
intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate is the literal command `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__evidence_io.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py tools/prove-gates.py`, which selects those three files. I read only the regions the diff touches, not the whole of the three suites. One flag, by reading: tests/test_stamp_verification.py:2056-2066, case sk1. It compares only the KEYS of _CLOCK_LITERALS_JUDGED with the literals found in the file (unjudged and stale sets), so a row whose reason text is false, as the old _BUILD_DELAY row was, would still pass. The truth of each reason is judged by the author alone. That is the known shape of a judged table and this task corrects the one row it was asked to; it is not a defect of the diff. Nothing else in the three touched regions would pass with its behaviour deleted: the tk2l skip is emitted only on the refusal branch, the tk2t check still compares the written key with M.tree_key(tree), and pw5 now asserts the registration identity.
